heading: Frequently asked questions
description: Everything you need to know before you put Helix to work on your repo.

items.question: What is Helix and how do I use it?
items.answer: Helix is an atomic work-breakdown orchestrator for AI coding agents. Describe the feature or fix you want, and Helix decomposes it into small, well-scoped units — each with its own acceptance criteria. Your coding agent then executes the units sequentially, so dependencies are always satisfied and every change ships clean.

items.question: How do I deploy and run Helix in my workflow?
items.answer: Helix runs locally as a CLI and plugs into the IDE or CI you already use. Point it at a repository, describe what you want shipped, and it returns a stack of atomic pull requests ready to review. There is nothing to host — Helix is an open-source orchestrator that sits between you and the agent.

items.question: What is the orchestration approach?
items.answer: Plan, execute, verify. Helix reads your intent and the codebase, produces an ordered list of units with clear scope, hands each unit to your agent with just-enough context, then type-checks, tests, and lints the result before it can move on. Failures pause the loop so nothing ships broken.

items.question: Who is Helix built for?
items.answer: Developers shipping features without reviewing 2,000-line AI diffs. Product managers who need predictable delivery they can report on. Founders who want velocity without late-night hotfixes. And enterprise teams who need governance, traceability, and the option to plug Helix into their own agent stack.

items.question: How is Helix different from a plain AI coding agent?
items.answer: Plain agents produce sprawling diffs with mixed quality. Helix enforces structure: every change is a small, scoped, verified unit. You get the speed of an AI agent with the reviewability of a human-sized PR — and a full audit trail of what shipped and why.

items.question: Can I bring my own coding agent?
items.answer: Yes. Helix is agent-agnostic. Point it at the agent you already trust — Claude, GPT, an in-house model — and Helix orchestrates the work. Bring your own keys, your own prompts, your own review policy.
